sources.title: Marine Debris Monitoring and Assessment Project
sources.sourcePeriod: ongoing shoreline surveys; each record date required
sources.uncertainty: Protocol and sampling effort must accompany each observation; absence of a survey is not zero debris.
sources.limitation: Shoreline macro-debris observations do not measure open-ocean concentration, river emissions, cleanup operations, or depth.

sources.authority: NOAA Office of Response and Restoration
sources.title: NOAA Marine Debris Monitoring and Assessment Project National Survey
sources.uncertainty: Candidate-site selection and accessibility metadata are not debris measurements.
sources.limitation: This is a national survey design/candidate-site layer, not a global debris observation field.

sources.title: The Great Pacific Garbage Patch
sources.sourcePeriod: multiple expeditions and models; page current when checked 2026-08-10
sources.uncertainty: The page summarizes modeled concentration and sampled vertical distribution but exposes no checked redistributable spatial package.
sources.limitation: Illustrations and summary values cannot be converted into atlas geometry without data access and reuse review.

sources.title: Seven years into the North Pacific garbage patch: legacy plastic fragments rising disproportionately faster than larger floating objects
sources.uncertainty: Publication reports trawl and aerial sampling plus a mass-balance model; reusable geospatial observations were not established in this prototype.
sources.limitation: A publication DOI is evidence context, not authorization to redistribute its underlying data or graphics.

sources.title: First evidence of plastic fallout from the North Pacific Garbage Patch
sources.sourcePeriod: published 2020; sample dates require article review
sources.uncertainty: The publication reports concentration decline with depth; station coordinates, sampling uncertainty, and reusable data package remain unverified.
sources.limitation: Depth observations from one North Pacific study cannot be generalized to every debris field.
